The finite certificate verifies this subgroup and its regular action; it does not supply a preferred point of I. title: Centralizer replaces normalizer
body: The normalizer of the normal Klein subgroup V is all of S4, whereas its centralizer is V itself; the two statements have different orders, 24 and 4. The same-line replacement therefore repairs a substantive group-theoretic assertion and makes the induced conjugation action of S4/V on V faithful. Exact permutation enumeration checks both orders, while Hua's §1 retains only the corrected centralizer statement.

title: An equivalence through reflections, not the automorphism-group functor
body: The construction D↦Q_D from the four noncentral involutions is fully faithful because its map Aut(D)→Aut(Q_D) is injective and both groups have order eight, and it is essentially surjective because every square has the same finite combinatorial type. The natural functor Q↦Aut(Q) instead has the central antipodism in the kernel of its map on automorphisms, so it cannot be that equivalence. Hua's §2 gives the same distinction; the finite enumeration verifies the eight reflection permutations and the two-element kernel, while scan017 itself exhibits the different square with vertices C⊔D.

A completed presentation may impose x²=a²=1, centrality of a, x′=ax, and the stated commutators, or use two adjacent involutions u,v with (uv)^4=1. The earlier prose says the x are involutions, so this is a gap in the written presentation rather than a refutation of the preceding equivalence; Hua's §2 repeats the presentation without supplying these missing relations.

The dual statement follows by interchanging vertices and edges, exactly as Hua's §2 Formulaire explains; these identities require two-element torsor structures, not only equal cardinalities.

On the standard module the certificate computes these quotient actions directly, finds a faithful ninety-six-element image, and identifies it with the full automorphism group of the target triple; since both groupoids of ordinary finite objects are connected, this proves equivalence in that setting. The construction is natural, whereas a chosen identification with a standard object is not, and extension to locally constant families additionally uses descent. title: A cohomological formulation of the square obstruction
body: Fix a locally constant torsor T under the constant finite group H=GL2(Λ)/{±I} on a specified topos B and its lifting through the stated constant central extension; put c=[ω_I], d=[C_Δ]=c+μ and μ=[Or(Δ)] in H¹(B,C2), so that any lifting square identifies c,d with [C_Q],[D_Q]. In the square quotient choose involutions a,b above(1,0),(0,1) with ab=zba and section q(x,y)=b^y a^x; its factor set is χ_c(g)χ_d(h), verified on all2304 quotient pairs, whose pullback gives the obstruction c∪d=c∪(c+μ) in H²(B,C2). When it vanishes, lifts equipped with an identification of their quotient with T form, up to isomorphism, a torsor under H¹(B,C2), and their automorphisms inducing the identity on T are H⁰(B,C2). Confidence is high for this scoped deduction from the checked cocycle and torsor descent, consistent with Ledet(2001,§0.4) after a coordinate change(for the field comparison, characteristic≠2), with no novelty or manuscript-attribution claim and no geometric or arithmetic base constructed here.

title: An explicit action that does not lift
body: The class of T=[[0,−1],[1,0]] in GL2(Λ)/{±I} has order two, while both lifts ±T square to −I. Sending the generator of C2 to this quotient class therefore gives an octahedral action with no C2-equivariant linear lift, proving the central extension is nonsplit. This does not say that an individual octahedron over the category of sets lacks some module representative; it shows that a coherent choice compatible with this action is impossible. Confidence is high because the two possible lifts and their squares are explicit and independently checked, refining Hua’s lifting discussion without claiming a counterexample to its groupoid theorem.
